close_reason: Deviation::new now returns Result<Self, DeviationAddError> with the same EmptyField checks DeviationStore::add applies (justification + authorized_by non-empty). The 'construct empty, serialize, round-trip, only fail at add' window is closed. Three regression tests lock the new contract (rejects empty justification, rejects empty authorized_by, new+add symmetry). Module-level doctest and two in-source callers updated. 293 pkix-lint tests pass; workspace builds clean. Commit landing.
description:
deviation.rs:225-242 Deviation::new accepts impl Into<String> for justification and authorized_by without validating non-emptiness. The validation happens only at DeviationStore::add time (deviation.rs:879-883).

Failure mode: a caller writes a config-driven Deviation builder that passes config strings directly to Deviation::new, gets back a valid-looking Deviation struct, and only discovers the empty-field error when finally calling store.add(). The Deviation can be inspected, serialized, even round-tripped through OSCAL — all without surfacing that it is unaddable.

Better shape: either (a) Deviation::new returns Result<Self, DeviationAddError> with the same EmptyField check applied at construction time, or (b) Deviation::new takes &str / NonEmptyString-like wrappers that prevent the misuse. The current shape lets the bug live in test fixtures, evidence packs, and OSCAL imports — anywhere a Deviation is constructed but not immediately added.

Maintainer consequence: future bug reports of the shape 'why does my deviation silently not apply' will trace back to this — somewhere up the call stack someone called Deviation::new('', '') and forgot to call store.add().
title: Deviation builder allows construction with empty justification/authorized_by but DeviationStore::add rejects
